messages:
Alex M.: Quick follow-up to the authn/authz RFC — we need to land on API key scoping semantics (project-scoped keys vs org-scoped wildcard keys). RFC favoured project-by-default, but infra asked for org keys. Need tradeoffs and next steps.

Mira S.: Strong +1 for project-by-default. Org keys are too blast-radiusy. We should allow org-wildcard only for an explicit 'infra' tier with approval and extra auditing.

Samir: Counterpoint — some infra agents (billing-exporter, quota-sync) legitimately need cross-project access. Maybe instead of full org keys we offer "constrained org keys" with an allow-list of routes/resources.

Jin Park: What about brokered delegation? Keep long-lived org keys only for humans/owners, and have a broker mint short-lived delegated tokens scoped to a project on demand. That avoids long-lived universal creds.

Kevin L.: Broker makes sense but increases surface area. We must ensure strong auditability: delegated tokens need claims that point back to the original principal, and we need rotation semantics that don't break rolling services.

Alex M.: Agreed. Minimal token claim set should include `actor_id` and `orig_key_id` so ACLs and audits can link requests. Rotation: org keys must rotate via KMS with env var + fallback pattern.

Mira S.: Also we need RBAC policy expressiveness: allow resource globs and "allowed_routes" so constrained org keys are actually enforceable. Example policy sketch: 

```json
{
  "principal": "svc:exporter-01",
  "scope": "project:proj-123",
  "claims": {
    "actor_id": "svc:infra-bot",
    "orig_key_id": "orgkey-09"
  },
  "exp": 1700000000
}
```

Samir: Don't forget quotas and rate-limits. We should enforce per-key quotas, and have per-project fallbacks so a noisy org key can't tank a single project.

auth-bot: Reminder: authn RFC v2 + follow-up notes at https://redwood/internal/rfc/authn-v2 (pinned).

Jin Park: Action items from this thread: 1) POC broker that mints delegated tokens and attaches `actor_id`/`orig_key_id`; 2) PR for policy grammar that supports constrained org keys and resource globs; 3) audit current org keys and owners, mark candidates for migration.

Alex M.: :thumbsup: I'll take (1) — will spin up a tiny POC service in eng-infra and demo the mint flow.

Kevin L.: I'll start the policy grammar PR. Proposed timeline: decision before next all-hands (~2 weeks). Is that realistic?

Mira S.: We should gate org-key creation behind a ticket + security review in the short term. Also add mandatory owner metadata on keys.

Samir: SGTM. One ask: ensure SDKs expose a helper `impersonate()` to request delegated tokens and transparently attach them to requests. Low friction for app teams.

Alex M.: Thanks everyone. I'll link notes and the POC tracker: https://redwood/notes/authn-followup-2248754321. Will update progress in #eng-infra and ping here for review.
